title: Standard morphisms and Pythagorean triples
summary: Let $m\geq 1$, let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z$ be a standard morphism and let $T(m)$ be the least integer $N$ such that every such $f$ admits a primitive monochromatic Pythagorean triple with hypotenuse at most $N$. The aim of this note is to prove that every standard morphism has infinitely many identity-valued Pythagorean triples and infinitely many primitive monochromatic Pythagorean triples.
